newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Burton sales, gross margin gain.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Burton sales, gross margin gain.

text.p: British clothing retailer Burton Group outlined current trading on Thursday which was broadly in line with expectations and said margins had improved.
But Burton shares slipped as investors took profits, analysts said.
Burton said total sales in the 20 weeks to January 18 were up 11.1 percent over a year ago while gross margin was up by one percentage point.
It said its department store chain Debenhams and womenswear unit Multiples saw sales rise a combined 7.3 percent in the period, and strong Christmas and New Year trading.
But it added that sales in menswear were "not as good."
Shares had slipped 6.25 pence to 155.5 pence by 1155 GMT.
"They've had a good run up recently and I think people are just ready to take some profits," said one market source.
"I couldn't see anything wrong in their statement," he added.

Burton shares have climbed about 5.4 percent over the last month and rose on Wednesday in a generally weaker retail sector after official figures showed UK retail sales fell 0.8 percent last month, which included the key Christmas trading period.
British retailers have been reporting mixed fortunes in Christmas sales leading analysts to suggest that a predicted pre-season spending boom failed to materialise.

Last week, retail chain Storehouse, which owns Bhs department stores and the Mothercare chain, said total sales were up nine percent in the six weeks to Christmas and the new year had got off to a good start.

But other stores have fared poorly, with catalogue retailer Argos warning that lower than expected sales and extra costs meant full year profits were unlikely to exceed the bottom end of expectations.
